source.title: Treating depression during pregnancy may benefit baby’s brain development – new research

key_claim: A short course of talk therapy for depressed pregnant women was linked to a smaller hippocampus in their babies, which was linked to calmer reactions at six months.

slides.headline: Therapy for mom may shape her baby's brain
Eight sessions of talk therapy
slides.body: Pregnant women with depression got MOMCare: eight 50-minute sessions on people skills, less conflict and more social support. Babies' brains were scanned within weeks of birth.

slides.headline: The catch: a smaller brain area
slides.body: The hippocampus, which helps with learning, memory and emotions, was 5% smaller in babies whose mothers got MOMCare. Smaller sounds bad.

slides.headline: Smaller may mean calmer
slides.body: Six months on, babies with a smaller hippocampus at birth tended to react less negatively to unfamiliar things. In infancy, faster brain growth may not always be better.

slides.headline: Helping a mother may help her baby too.
slides.body: The authors say it helps mother and baby. Long-term effects are still unknown.

caption:
Therapy for mom may shape her baby's brain

A new study tested MOMCare, a short course of talk therapy, on pregnant women with depression. It was eight 50-minute sessions. The babies' brains were scanned within weeks of birth.

The catch? The hippocampus, a brain area tied to learning, memory and emotions, was 5% smaller in babies whose mothers got MOMCare. In infancy, faster growth may not always be better.

The payoff? Six months later, babies with a smaller hippocampus at birth tended to respond less negatively to unfamiliar things. The authors plan to keep following the children. 🧠

Source: The Conversation — Treating depression during pregnancy may benefit baby’s brain development – new research
